rules.rule: Foundation services must serve only one entity type.
Foundation services must perform structural and logical validation on all incoming models.
Foundation services must call only brokers — never another service.
Foundation services must not enrich a model with business data. Audit stamping through the security audit broker is required, not a violation.
Foundation services must map broker exceptions to local exceptions using dependency validation wrappers.
Foundation services must wrap all broker calls in try-catch blocks.
Foundation services must be partial classes split by concern (.cs, .Substrate.cs, .Validations.cs, .Exceptions.cs), not by operation category.
Foundation service interfaces must follow the naming pattern I{Entity}Service.
Foundation services must take the acting identity from the inbound envelope's SecurityContext and pass it explicitly to every audit and user-id call — never an ambient accessor.
Foundation services must enforce their own security; no layer may assume an upstream layer already gated the caller.
Event-path handlers must verify the envelope's integrity signature in the receiver, against the handler's event name and the request direction.
A read the caller may not perform must answer not-found, never unauthorized; the true denial reason is logged server-side only.

Every operation that has a request address (Adding, Modifying, RemovingById, HardRemovingById, RetrievingById) must be reachable both directly and via the substrate, converging on one private DoXAsync. RetrieveAll has no request address and is deliberately excluded.
Mutating event handlers must check ProcessedEvents before acting and record both the inbound request id and the outbound fact id after; a deduplicated delivery replies null.
Event-path handlers must always rethrow after categorizing so the substrate records the delivery as Error and drives retries.
